column2: How is blood glucose maintained early in an overnight fast while glucose is also spared?
column3: Liver glycogen supplies much glucose as gluconeogenesis rises; falling insulin and rising glucagon permit lipolysis, so muscle and liver oxidise more fat, while glycerol, lactate and alanine feed gluconeogenesis.

column2: Why does rising ketone availability protect muscle protein during prolonged fasting?
column3: Ketones let the brain reduce glucose use, lowering the need to convert muscle protein into glucose, since sustained protein loss would be incompatible with survival.

column2: Why does hepatic ketogenesis accelerate when fatty-acid oxidation is high?
column3: Oxaloacetate is diverted to gluconeogenesis and high NADH slows cycle reactions, so acetyl-CoA exceeds citric-acid-cycle capacity and is routed via HMG-CoA synthase and lyase to acetoacetate.

column2: Why does the liver export ketone bodies but cannot use them?
column3: It lacks succinyl-CoA:acetoacetate CoA-transferase (thiophorase), which extrahepatic mitochondria use to activate acetoacetate with succinyl-CoA before splitting it into two acetyl units for oxidation.

column2: What distinguishes physiological nutritional ketosis from ketoacidosis?
column3: In nutritional ketosis, preserved insulin restrains runaway lipolysis so ketonaemia stays limited and pH is regulated; ketoacidosis arises when production overwhelms utilisation and buffering amid hormonal dysregulation.

column2: How does severe insulin deficiency drive ketogenesis in diabetic ketoacidosis?
column3: With excess glucagon and stress hormones, adipose lipolysis floods the liver with fatty acids, malonyl-CoA falls, and mitochondrial fatty-acid entry and ketogenesis accelerate.

column2: Why is total-body potassium depleted in diabetic ketoacidosis even when serum potassium is normal or high?
column3: Osmotic diuresis causes electrolyte loss, while insulin deficiency, acidosis and hyperosmolality shift potassium out of cells, so the serum value hides the depletion.

column2: Why is glucose added during treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis once blood glucose falls?
column3: Insulin is given to stop ketogenesis, and ketones are still being cleared after glucose falls, so glucose is added to let insulin continue.

column2: Why does alcoholic ketoacidosis favour beta-hydroxybutyrate, and why is dextrose given with thiamine?
column3: Ethanol-induced high NADH, with low glycogen, low insulin and lipolysis, favours beta-hydroxybutyrate; dextrose stimulates insulin, and thiamine is given before or with carbohydrate in at-risk patients.

column2: Why can urine nitroprusside testing mislead both in severe ketoacidosis and during recovery?
column3: It detects acetoacetate more than beta-hydroxybutyrate; high NADH in severe illness shifts the pool to beta-hydroxybutyrate, underestimating severity, and reconversion during recovery keeps urine ketones high despite improvement.

column2: Why is refeeding after severe deprivation dangerous even though food is not a toxin?
column3: The metabolic transition triggers insulin-driven shifts of phosphate, potassium and magnesium and raises thiamine demand; severe hypophosphataemia impairs heart, respiratory muscle, blood cells and nervous system.

column2: How can insulin resistance worsen hepatic steatosis when insulin normally promotes lipogenesis?
column3: Insulin resistance can increase fatty-acid delivery from adipose tissue while hepatic lipogenesis remains insulin responsive, so uptake plus synthesis exceed oxidation plus lipoprotein export.

column2: What distinguishes adrenoleukodystrophy from Zellweger-spectrum disorders at the peroxisome?
column3: Adrenoleukodystrophy impairs peroxisomal transport of very-long-chain fatty acids, whereas Zellweger-spectrum disorders impair peroxisome assembly and so disrupt multiple pathways, causing severe multisystem disease.

column2: Why is pharmacological activation of brown and beige fat challenging?
column3: These tissues dissipate energy as heat through uncoupling protein 1 under sympathetic stimulation, but systemic adrenergic effects and compensatory appetite can offset the added expenditure.
